proof:
Conventions.
- ℚ ⊆ ℝ via the cast q ↦ (q : ℝ). 'For all sufficiently large j' means eventually along atTop on ℕ.
- ℝ^ℚ is the space of functions ℚ → ℝ with the product topology, in which convergence is pointwise convergence (tendsto_pi_nhds).
- Hypotheses: each F_j : ℝ → ℝ is nondecreasing, and |F_j(t)| ≤ C for all j ∈ ℕ and t ∈ ℝ.

Source: the parent proof (P6), step 2 ('Helly selection') and the first half of step 6, applied to an arbitrary uniformly bounded sequence of nondecreasing functions. In the parent, F_j(t) = M_{W ∩ {φ < t}}(X_j) as a real number.
- The parent's diagonal argument over ℚ is realized as sequential compactness of a countable product of compact intervals.
- The parent's exceptional set {F⁻ < F⁺} is replaced by the countable set of discontinuity points of the monotone function F⁻, which contains it (remark after step 5).

Proof.
1. (The compact box.)
   - Let K := ∏_{q∈ℚ}[−C, C] = {g ∈ ℝ^ℚ : −C ≤ g(q) ≤ C for all q}. K is compact by Tychonoff's theorem (isCompact_univ_pi applied to isCompact_Icc).
   - For j ∈ ℕ put G_j(q) := F_j(q) for q ∈ ℚ. Since |F_j(q)| ≤ C means −C ≤ F_j(q) ≤ C (abs_le), every G_j lies in K.
2. (Diagonal extraction.)
   - ℚ is countable and ℝ is first countable, so the product ℝ^ℚ is first countable.
   - Hence every sequence in the compact set K has a subsequence converging to a point of K (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). This gives g ∈ K and a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with G_{ψ(j)} → g in ℝ^ℚ.
   - Convergence in the product topology is pointwise convergence, so F_{ψ(j)}(q) → g(q) as j → ∞ for every q ∈ ℚ.
   - g(q) ≤ C for every q, because g ∈ K.
3. (g is nondecreasing on ℚ.) Let q ≤ q′ in ℚ. Then (q : ℝ) ≤ (q′ : ℝ), so F_{ψ(j)}(q) ≤ F_{ψ(j)}(q′) for every j, because F_{ψ(j)} is nondecreasing. Limits preserve non-strict inequalities (le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'), so g(q) ≤ g(q′).
4. (The left envelope F⁻.) For t ∈ ℝ let Q_t := {q ∈ ℚ : (q : ℝ) < t}.
   - Q_t is nonempty, since some rational lies below t (exists_rat_lt), and g ≤ C on Q_t.
   - So F⁻(t) := sup_{q ∈ Q_t} g(q) is a well-defined real number: a conditionally complete supremum of a nonempty set bounded above.
   F⁻ has the following properties.
   (a) If q ∈ ℚ, t ∈ ℝ and (q : ℝ) < t, then g(q) ≤ F⁻(t), because q ∈ Q_t (le_ciSup).
   (b) If q ∈ ℚ, t ∈ ℝ and t ≤ (q : ℝ), then F⁻(t) ≤ g(q). Every q′ ∈ Q_t satisfies q′ < t ≤ q, so g(q′) ≤ g(q) by step 3. Since Q_t ≠ ∅, the supremum is at most g(q) (ciSup_le).
   (c) F⁻ is nondecreasing on ℝ. If t ≤ t′, every q ∈ Q_t satisfies (q : ℝ) < t ≤ t′, so g(q) ≤ F⁻(t′) by (a). Taking the supremum over the nonempty Q_t gives F⁻(t) ≤ F⁻(t′).
5. (The exceptional set.)
   - Let E := {s ∈ ℝ : F⁻ is not continuous at s}.
   - F⁻ : ℝ → ℝ is monotone by 4(c), so its set of discontinuity points is countable (Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt). Hence E is countable.
   - Remark, not used below: E contains the parent's jump set {s : F⁻(s) < F⁺(s)}, where F⁺(s) := inf_{q ∈ ℚ, q > s} g(q). Indeed, let F⁻ be continuous at s. For every real t > s and every rational q with s < q < t, F⁺(s) ≤ g(q) ≤ F⁻(t) by (a). Letting t ↓ s gives F⁺(s) ≤ F⁻(s), and F⁻(s) ≤ F⁺(s) follows from step 3.
6. (Small increments of g near s ∉ E.) Let s ∉ E and ε > 0.
   - F⁻ is continuous at s, so there is δ > 0 with |F⁻(t) − F⁻(s)| < ε/4 whenever |t − s| < δ.
   - By density of ℚ, choose rationals a, b with s − δ < a < s and s < b < s + δ/2. Then:
     - g(b) ≤ F⁻(s + δ/2) by 4(a), since b < s + δ/2;
     - F⁻(a) ≤ g(a) by 4(b) with t = a;
     - |F⁻(s + δ/2) − F⁻(s)| < ε/4 and |F⁻(a) − F⁻(s)| < ε/4, since both points lie within δ of s.
   - Hence g(b) − g(a) ≤ F⁻(s + δ/2) − F⁻(a) ≤ |F⁻(s + δ/2) − F⁻(s)| + |F⁻(s) − F⁻(a)| < ε/2.
7. (Passing to the subsequence.)
   - By step 2, F_{ψ(j)}(b) → g(b) and F_{ψ(j)}(a) → g(a), so F_{ψ(j)}(b) − F_{ψ(j)}(a) → g(b) − g(a) < ε/2 < ε.
   - Since (−∞, ε) is a neighbourhood of the limit (gt_mem_nhds), F_{ψ(j)}(b) − F_{ψ(j)}(a) < ε for all sufficiently large j.
8. (Conclusion.)
   - ψ is strictly increasing (step 2), and E is countable (step 5).
   - For every s ∉ E and every ε > 0, the reals a < s < b of step 6 satisfy F_{ψ(j)}(b) − F_{ψ(j)}(a) < ε for all sufficiently large j (step 7). ∎
key_steps: Tychonoff and first countability of ℝ^ℚ: the restrictions F_j|_ℚ lie in the compact box ∏_{q∈ℚ}[−C,C], so a strictly increasing ψ gives F_{ψ(j)}(q) → g(q) for every rational q.
g is nondecreasing on ℚ. F⁻(t) := sup_{q<t} g(q) is a well-defined nondecreasing real function with g(q) ≤ F⁻(t) for q < t and F⁻(t) ≤ g(q) for t ≤ q.
E := the set of discontinuity points of the monotone F⁻ is countable (Monotone.countable_not_continuousAt).
For s ∉ E, continuity of F⁻ at s gives rationals a < s < b with g(b) − g(a) ≤ F⁻(s+δ/2) − F⁻(a) < ε/2.
Pointwise convergence along ψ gives F_{ψ(j)}(b) − F_{ψ(j)}(a) < ε for all sufficiently large j.
